extraction_status.description: How much of the source document was captured. COMPLETE = everything the document specified was captured. PARTIAL = the document did not specify some things, so they were left empty and listed in extraction_notes; this is the normal result for a work-in-progress doc and is not an error. LIMITED = a config file, schema or the validator was unavailable, so part of the run had less grounding than usual — see extraction_notes. Not COMPLETE whenever extraction_notes is non-empty.

extraction_notes.description: Things the source document did not say, recorded instead of guessing a value. An empty array means nothing was left open. A non-empty array is normal and expected on a work-in-progress document — it is a to-do list for the author, not a list of errors.

field.description: JSON path of the field left empty, e.g. business_requirements[3].target_module. Use 'ENVIRONMENT' for tool or install issues not tied to one field.

reason.description: What was checked and what was found there, e.g. 'PRD section 4.2 states the rule but names no module'.

action.description: The concrete next step, e.g. 'confirm the target module with the PM'.

follow_up.description: How much attention this needs. NEEDS_ANSWER = someone has to supply this before the tests can cover it. WORTH_CHECKING = a value was produced, but without its usual reference source, so confirm it. FYI = optional content the document simply does not have; no action needed.

unmapped_extractor_data.description: Catch-all for anything the extractors produced that no other field in this schema accommodates. The generator NEVER drops extractor data — whatever it cannot place elsewhere is copied here verbatim, so the plan is a lossless superset of its inputs. Keyed by source (prd / rfc / design / plan); each value holds the un-placed fields exactly as received. Empty object when everything mapped cleanly. Downstream may ignore it, but it must never be the reason information was lost.

coverage_categories.description: Output of the Test-Category Selection Gate (Step 0). auto_selected is the mandatory signal-derived baseline; optional_extras are QA-discretionary.

auto_selected.description: Categories whose detection signal fired in the supplied contexts. Always generated.

reason.description: The exact input field that fired, e.g. rfc.lifecycle_considerations[0].event = PROCESS_DEATH

feature_adjacent.description: Categories whose trigger field exists in the schema but was empty/absent for this feature.

fe_baseline.description: Universal FE-mobile hygiene categories not derivable from the docs, gated by an applicability predicate.

user_removed.description: AUTO categories the QA explicitly overrode out of scope, with reason.

coverage_category.description: Which Category Catalog category this scenario belongs to (e.g. boundary, interruption_network, session_auth).

source.description: Provenance of the scenario. fe_baseline/qa_added are curated hygiene, NOT input-derived requirements.

steps.description: Supports automated execution steps and manual/legacy regression test steps.

clickstream_events.description: Clickstream/analytics telemetry specs extracted from prd-extractor.

test_data.description: One entry per test-data fixture the scenario needs. Carries the full structured state assembled from PRD (target_personas, prerequisites, boundary_conditions) and RFC (flags, N-1, api/state changes) — NOT flattened to tag strings. This is the identification input for the downstream test-data-generation stage.

fixture_id.description: Stable id for this fixture, reused across scenarios that need the same entity/state so downstream can dedup, e.g. 'fixture-kyced-gopay-user'.

entity.description: Test-data domain/entity, e.g. CUSTOMER, DRIVER, VOUCHER, PAYMENT_INSTRUMENT. From the persona/requirement, not invented.

description.description: Human-readable description of the fixture, verbatim or normalised from the PRD persona/prerequisite.

required_state.description: Structured state predicates the entity must satisfy, e.g. {"kyc_status":"VERIFIED","gopay_active":true}. Assembled from target_personas.prerequisites + boundary_conditions. Static entity attributes ONLY — see dynamic_conditions for temporal/relational needs. Empty object if the source states an entity but no attributes.

type_signals.description: Short signal labels for this fixture (the former test_data_tags), e.g. ['kyc_verified_user','birthday_d_day']. Downstream maps these to test_data_type_signals. Signals summarise; required_state is the source of truth.

condition.description: Plain-language condition that is NOT a static entity attribute, e.g. 'current date equals the customer date_of_birth' for a birthday trigger. Kept out of required_state because no static category can match it.

items.description: Conditions that are relationships or time-based rather than stored attributes — birthday-on-D-day, N-th transaction, clock-dependent. These become selection constraints or operations downstream, never required_state predicates.

provision.description: How the fixture is expected to be provisioned. Omit if unknown at plan time.

sensitive.description: True for KYC identity, card, or PII state that must be synthetic, never real prod data.

count.description: How many distinct instances of this fixture the scenario needs. Default 1 if omitted.

source_refs.description: What this fixture traces to — PRD req_id / persona type / boundary_condition id / RFC flag_key. Keeps every fixture auditable back to a real source field.
